fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The occult is psychology wearing a mask", "body": "Chance Garton opens by arguing that whatever is real in what people call the occult, the hidden, is simply psychology, the psyche of the individual, the collective, and the universe itself. He points out that you cannot separate the most famous psychologists of the modern age from myth and the hidden arts. Freud wrote Moses and Monotheism, Jung wrote endlessly about alchemy and the image making faculty of consciousness. From there he frames mythographers, priest classes, kings and tyrants as masters of universal psychology who either play to a people's strengths or prey upon their weaknesses."}, {"title": "Gurdjieff, the Sufis, and the beehive", "body": "Gabriel, who goes by Slick Dissident, walks through the Enneagram's contested history. It reaches the modern world through Gurdjieff, who credited a Sufi sect whose name translates roughly as the keepers of the bees. Gabriel finds that thrilling because the Beehive Cluster sits in Cancer, which he ties to the Chariot card and its gilded gold. A rival lineage claims independent South American discovery. The personality matrix, he notes, was layered onto the older figure fairly recently, which is why the system now lives mostly in self help circles rather than initiate ones."}, {"title": "How the nine numbers actually divide", "body": "The heart of the episode is the map. The big Y splits the circle into three trines. Eights, nines and ones are instinct, body and the present moment. Twos, threes and fours are feeling and the past. Fives, sixes and sevens are thinking and the future, and the four to five crossing is the pivot of the whole figure. A second grouping sorts the numbers into compliant, aggressive and withdrawn. Gabriel adds that the seven deadly sins form the base, with deceit and fear added for three and six, and that dividing almost any number by seven yields 142857 repeating."}, {"title": "Star Wars as a tarot deck in motion", "body": "Gabriel's project overlays the Thoth Crowley tarot and Star Wars onto the nine stations. Luke Skywalker is the Fool and the perfectionist one, alongside Athena and her shadow brother Ares, and Zeus when he must fight Typhon. Chewbacca is the Magi and the giver, always repairing, always saying yes, a willing slave whose pride roars. Princess Leia and Dionysus hold the achiever three with its shadow of deceit. Han Solo, married to the Empress as the Millennium Falcon, is the emperor and the individual four, driven by envy. Obi Wan Kenobi sits at five, the observer."}, {"title": "Feeding the demon of a number", "body": "Both men keep returning to how this knowledge could be used against people. Chance Garton describes collectivism as the shadow of oneness and traces it through the one percent slogan, MAGA loyalty that survived Warp Speed, and January 6th, arguing that righteous indignation is the easiest lever for moving crowds. He predicts pride parades oscillating into wrath parades. Gabriel goes further, suggesting that childhood images like Chewbacca choking Lando Calrissian can be summoned decades later around events like George Floyd. Their closing warning, echoing The Prisoner, is blunt. You are not a number."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Slick Dissident, the symbolic syncretism master sleuth, returns to InnerVerse for a deep dive into the esoteric enneagram. We'll be exploring the light and shadow archetypes of the nine divines, and exploring the digital significance of such knowledge being used by occultists over the long spans of human existence.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we continue analyzing the enneagram, using Star Wars and mythology as our frameworks for allegorical understanding. It's a huge 1.5+ hour extension!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Observer and the many faces of greed", "body": "Slick Dissident places the Observer at station five of the Enneagram, shadowed by greed, and links it to Mammon, uneven weights and measures, and getting one up on your fellow man. He reads Obi-Wan Kenobi as this type, hoarding his years in hiding and even, as both hosts put it, greedily taking the blame for Vader's fall. Chance Garton widens the idea, suggesting a person can be greedy for blame, recognition or status as easily as for wealth, and admits that students of these subjects can grow hungrier for knowledge the more of it they take in."}, {"title": "Tarot cards Gabriel sees inside Star Wars", "body": "Slick Dissident argues that the Thoth Hierophant card mirrors the scene where Obi-Wan receives Leia's message: C-3PO's eyes go dark like the card's masked creatures while R2-D2 projects a small image of the divine feminine, which he compares to Isis. He then ties the Aeon card to Edvard Munch's The Scream, which he connects to the red skies after Krakatoa, and to Obi-Wan sensing Alderaan's destruction, framing the Aeon's hushing gesture as the answer to a scream. Chance Garton flips the sequence, asking whether Krakatoa might itself have been a response rather than the original call."}, {"title": "Loyalty, fear, and the divine twins", "body": "Slick Dissident pairs the loyalist, the number six, with Apollo and casts its shadow of fear as Artemis, the twin who guards the wilderness beyond the city. In his reading, Apollonian people thrive on rules and order, while Artemis rules the unpredictable edges, and he sees smart cities and social media platforms as modern cities of loyalty kept in line by fear. Chance Garton adds the goddess Themis, suggesting loyalists cling to law and order because it feels just, and offers the image of fear as a dam that blocks the natural flow a loyalist would otherwise follow."}, {"title": "Gabriel's Enneagram reading of world leaders", "body": "Slick Dissident explains that the project began as a reverse psychological profile of world leaders, inspired by his understanding that Allen Dulles brought Carl Jung in to profile the Nazis. He places Barack Obama at the enthusiast, Donald Trump at the Challenger and Joe Biden at the slothful nine, and speculates that the sequence could point to Tulsi Gabbard as a perfectionist figure next. He presents these as archetypal readings rather than proof. Chance Garton suggests he test the pattern against past presidents and cites the old line that politics is show business for ugly people."}, {"title": "Sight beyond the ordinary spectrum", "body": "Slick Dissident brings up tetrachromacy, the ability some people have to perceive a wider range of color, and floats his own theory that it may be passed on through certain birth rituals. Chance Garton reads the definition aloud, noting that humans normally have three types of cone cells, and wonders aloud whether some rituals involving the eyes could relate to altered vision. The two speculate that heightened sight might be trained spiritually, and Slick Dissident imagines an elite class of astronomer priests, which Chance Garton ties back to the Observer's greed and the hoarding of knowledge once shared openly."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I believe personally that when we talk about the quote unquote occult, the hidden, if we are describing something real, we are talking about psychology, the psychology, the psyche of humanity, the collective, the individual, the world and the universe itself", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It's like architecture or like a loose substructure of the shape of the collective mind. And it's been given a particular shape such that I think later in our lives, they can hit these notes in these similar echoes to the shape of these archetypes. And it will ring true to us because it was seeded into our youth.", "author": "Slick Dissident", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "So he attributed the Enneagram to a Sufi sect. And the name of those Sufis is something like Sardegos or Sarrogues. It translates to the keepers of the bees. And that is quite fascinating to me because the beehive cluster is in the cancer constellation.", "author": "Slick Dissident", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "Up to 50% of the world population identifies as the six. And that single fact alone is really monumental, and it also bespeaks of social engineering quite pronouncedly because the sixes are very conveniently loyalists, and their shadow aspect is to be fearful.", "author": "Slick Dissident", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "And so a person who is expressing wrathful or angry behavior is very simply looking for perfection. They're demanding something better. And it's just as simple as that. A lot of people make the mistake of thinking of anger as being hateful. And that just is not true.", "author": "Slick Dissident", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "So my point is that this collectivism is really easily instilled and exploited in people when you're playing on their wrath side. When you get them all riled up, like, there's very few emotional switches that work for the movement of mass action in a certain direction, like righteous indignation.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And so maybe that's also kind of related to the deceit aspect of it that the two mother when pregnant and the child is within her is carrying, the two is carrying the three but it's hidden, you know, and deceit and hiding go together.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "As fascinating, as educational as it is to learn these systems, I do have good reason to believe that what happens when we all attach to these archetypes and they standardize the symbols of our childhood psychological scaffolding, the nefariousness is that these things can be triggered and called up and summoned later on in your life.", "author": "Slick Dissident", "portrait": ""}]
